items.quote: The Grand Ole Opry is a regular live country-music radio broadcast originating from Nashville, Tennessee, on WSM
items.note: Founded 28 Nov 1925 as the WSM Barn Dance, 'taking its current name in 1927'; the article treats 1925 as the Opry's start. Minor: it now airs 'between two and five nights per week', so 'weekly' is loose but not wrong.

items.quote: The Parthenon in Centennial Park, Nashville, Tennessee, United States, is a full-scale replica of the original Parthenon in Athens
It is served atop slices of white bread with pickle chips
The logo was a reference to a partial Smilodon skeleton found beneath downtown Nashville in 1971 during construction of the First American National Bank building
items.note: Rewording fixed the giveaway: the team is now named in the question and the fossil is what is asked. Same article: 'a saber-toothed cat (Smilodon fatalis)'. Accept 'sabre-toothed tiger'; the team name hints 'predator' but not the species.

items.quote: Originally known as the Houston Oilers, the team was founded in 1959
items.note: They played 1997-98 as the Tennessee Oilers, but the question asks for the pre-move Houston name, so only Oilers fits.

items.quote: Vanderbilt's intercollegiate athletics teams are nicknamed the Commodores
Elected President in 1828, Jackson enlarged the Hermitage during his first term
items.note: Lead: '10 mi east of downtown Nashville in the neighborhood of Hermitage', so 'outside Nashville' is fair (it is inside Metro Nashville-Davidson County, but outside the city proper).

items.quote: The singers were organized as a fundraising effort for Fisk University
items.note: 'The first group was organized in 1871 to tour and raise funds for college.' The group is usually called the FISK Jubilee Singers; the question rightly omits 'Fisk'.

items.quote: The district is centered on 16th and 17th Avenues South (called Music Square East and Music Square West, respectively, within the Music Row area)
items.note: 'Two-word name' is a hint, not a giveaway. A room might offer 'Music Square' (the avenues' names inside the district); host should not accept it.

items.quote: It includes Lower Broadway, a tourist and entertainment district renowned for honky tonks and live country music
